what: Viatris is a generic and established-brand pharmaceutical company formed from Mylan and Pfizer's off-patent business. It supplies medicines to around a billion patients a year across most countries.
customers: Pharmacies, wholesalers, hospitals and government health systems worldwide.
money: generic and established brands in North America and Europe
Greater China, JANZ and Emerging Markets
the same portfolio across Asia and emerging markets
moat: Manufacturing scale across thousands of products and regulatory approvals in most countries, which lets it supply medicines at prices smaller producers cannot match.
risks: It reported a loss after writing down the value of acquired products
Revenue has fallen about 4% a year over three years
Debt of about $14 billion against under $2 billion of cash
Generic pricing in the United States remains under pressure
opportunities: A dividend yield around 2.4% while debt is reduced
Gross margin of 35% leaves room if the product mix improves
A pipeline of complex generics and biosimilars earns better margins than plain generics
watch: Debt reduction and whether revenue stabilises in developed markets.
